source.authors: Lanfang Sun, Emi Kawano-Yamashita, Takashi Nagata, Hisao Tsukamoto, Yuji Furutani, Mitsumasa Koyanagi, Akihisa Terakita
source.title: Distribution of Mammalian-Like Melanopsin in Cyclostome Retinas Exhibiting a Different Extent of Visual Functions

where: Results, Spectroscopic characterization and photosensitivity of the melanopsins
method: absorption spectrum of recombinant lamprey melanopsin expressed in COS-1 cells, reconstituted with 11-cis retinal, purified on 1D4-agarose, recorded at 10 C with a Shimadzu UV-2450; value given as approximate
conditions: Not a native retinal measurement: the melanopsin cDNA of the river lamprey (animals supplied by a university colleague; the paper does not say whether they were wild-caught) was expressed in cultured COS-1 cells, the protein reconstituted with 11-cis retinal, detergent-extracted and purified, and its dark-state spectrum recorded at 10 C. The paper gives no replicate count for the spectrum and no fit statistic, and states the value as 'approximately'. The Abstract does not give the number (it says only that the recombinant pigment is blue light-sensitive). A hagfish (Eptatretus burgeri) melanopsin could not be purified, so no hagfish spectrum is reported. The paper reports no photoreceptor (rod or cone) lambda max and no behavioural light response; Ca2+ imaging with 500 ms blue light (12 cells, Fig 2 legend) is a separate result not filed.
quote: The absorption maximum of the lamprey melanopsin was approximately 480 nm …
note: Sentence cut after the value; cut text begins with the figure reference '(Fig. 2A)' and continues ', indicating that it is a blue light-sensitive pigment...' (tail past the clause not read). The cut drops no qualifier of the 480 nm; 'approximately' kept. Start of the sentence confirmed by a second pass (first words 'The absorption maximum of the lamprey melanopsin was'; the preceding sentence ends 'were unable to obtain a purified hagfish melanopsin'). New trait for this species (no Lethenteron or DOI hit anywhere in docs/ or in desk-d23*/d24* evidence). Family and order as filed on main for Petromyzontidae (Petromyzontiformes); the name Lethenteron camtschaticum is not in gbif-names.tsv, WoRMS/OBIS not opened (refused). Licence: page prints 'Creative Commons Attribution License'; Crossref lists CC BY 4.0 with content-version unspecified (accepted pairing). Crossref authors (7), volume 9, issue 9 and year 2014 agree with the page.

source.authors: Leo Peichl, Sonja Meimann, Irina Solovei, Irene L. Gügel, Christina Geiger, Nicole Schauerte, Karolina Goździewska-Harłajczuk, Joanna E. Klećkowska-Nawrot, Gudrun Wibbelt, Silke Haverkamp
source.title: Eye features and retinal photoreceptors of the nocturnal aardvark (Orycteropus afer, Tubulidentata)

method: external eye dimensions of one fixed eye (aardvark 1); approximate value; the text adds that the axial length is probably an underestimate because the cornea had collapsed
conditions: Two zoo aardvarks that had died of natural causes: aardvark 1, a nearly 25-year-old male whose right eye was removed one day post mortem and immersion-fixed in 4% formalin for 24 h at 4 C; aardvark 2, a nearly 6-year-old female whose eyes were enucleated immediately after death and fixed in buffered formaldehyde (a third animal was used only for serum thyroid hormone). Most findings in the paper come from aardvark 1. External eye dimensions were recorded after fixation. n = 1 eye for the axial length; the paper gives no mean or range for the species.
quote: The eye of aardvark 1 had an equatorial diameter of approx. 23.0 mm and an axial length of approx. 21.2 mm.
note: Whole Results sentence (20 words), read in full in one piece. Value is the single eye's 'approx.' axial length, measured after fixation in a 25-year-old captive male; the paper states the figure is likely an underestimate (collapsed cornea), which is a qualifier in a neighbouring sentence and is given here. Not a species mean. New trait for this species: eye_axial_length_mm is a key already on main (e.g. Molothrus ater, Hippopotamus amphibius) though absent from the checker list. Family Orycteropodidae from iNaturalist/GBIF titles returned by search ('Aardvarks (Family Orycteropodidae)'); order Tubulidentata as printed in the paper; name Orycteropus afer accepted (GBIF species page returned by search). No Orycteropus or this DOI anywhere in docs/ or desk-d23*/d24* evidence. Licence: page prints 'Creative Commons Attribution License'; Crossref CC BY 4.0, content-version vor. Crossref authors (10), volume 20, issue 3, year 2025 agree.

value: reflective tapetum lucidum with features of a choroidal tapetum fibrosum; retinal pigment epithelium in front of it unpigmented

source.authors: Leo Peichl, Sonja Meimann, Irina Solovei, Irene L. Gügel, Christina Geiger, Nicole Schauerte, Karolina Goździewska-Harłajczuk, Joanna E. Klećkowska-Nawrot, Gudrun Wibbelt, Silke Haverkamp
source.title: Eye features and retinal photoreceptors of the nocturnal aardvark (Orycteropus afer, Tubulidentata)

method: gross eye inspection and histology of fixed eyes of two zoo aardvarks; Figure 4 (choroid and tapetum) is labelled aardvark 1
conditions: Two zoo aardvarks that had died of natural causes: aardvark 1, a nearly 25-year-old male whose right eye was removed one day post mortem and immersion-fixed in 4% formalin for 24 h at 4 C; aardvark 2, a nearly 6-year-old female whose eyes were enucleated immediately after death and fixed in buffered formaldehyde (a third animal was used only for serum thyroid hormone). Most findings in the paper come from aardvark 1. External eye dimensions were recorded after fixation. n = 1 eye for the axial length; the paper gives no mean or range for the species. The paper states 'in contrast to some previous studies' (earlier reports had denied a tapetum). The Results sentence 'This bright band had the appearance of a tapetum lucidum, its dorso-ventral width was larger in the temporal than the nasal...' was read to 125 characters only. The paper does not say which animal each histological statement rests on beyond the Figure 4 caption.
quote: In contrast to some previous studies, we found that the aardvark eye has a reflective tapetum lucidum with features of a choroidal tapetum fibrosum, in front of which the retinal pigment epithelium is unpigmented.
note: Whole Abstract sentence (33 words) read verbatim in two abutting pieces in one response ('...reflective tapetum lucidum' | 'with features of a choroidal tapetum fibrosum, in front of ... unpigmented.') and joined identically on a second pass. Value is the sentence's own claim, a presence finding. Same source, licence and Crossref check as the axial-length record; not on main for this species.
